column3: The Hebrew does not explicitly add above before the cherubim as BSB does.
The Hebrew uses thanksgiving rather than praise.
The Hebrew makes the king’s strength the subject loving justice; BSB makes the mighty King the subject.
The Hebrew uses a participle for calling and an uncompleted verb for answering; BSB uses past verbs.
The Hebrew has statute in the singular and in a pillar of cloud; BSB has statutes and from the pillar.
The Hebrew joins forgiveness and vengeance with and; BSB uses yet and explicitly calls the deeds misdeeds.
